facts.claim: Vaswani and colleagues introduced the Transformer in 2017, a network built on attention alone, dropping the building blocks earlier language networks relied on (recurrence and convolutions).
Meta’s Llama 3 report (2024): its largest model has 405 billion learned numbers, 126 layers of 128 heads, vectors of 16,384 numbers, a vocabulary of 128,000 tokens and a window of up to 128K tokens.
Vaswani and colleagues (2017) compute attention as softmax(QKᵀ / √d_k) V: each token’s query is scored against every key, the scores become weights that add up to 1, and the weights mix the values.
Vaswani and colleagues (2017) mask attention in the part of the Transformer that writes, so a position cannot look at the positions after it and each prediction depends only on what came before.
Multi-head attention runs several heads side by side, so the model can attend to different kinds of information at once.

Voita and colleagues (2019) found that the most important heads in a translation Transformer play consistent, often nameable roles; removing 38 of the 48 heads that read the input cost only 0.15 points of translation score (BLEU).
The original base Transformer used 8 heads and a stack of 6 layers.
Rotary position embedding (RoPE), from Su and colleagues, encodes a token's position with a rotation, so attention also reflects how far apart two tokens are.
Nucleus (top-p) sampling, from Holtzman and colleagues, draws from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to at least p.
Holtzman and colleagues (2019) found that picking text for its likelihood, as greedy picking does, gives text that is bland and strangely repetitive, even from a strong model.
Holtzman and colleagues note that lowering the temperature improves quality but costs diversity.

Holtzman and colleagues describe sampling with temperature as dividing the model’s raw scores by the temperature before turning them into probabilities; a temperature below 1 skews them toward the likeliest tokens.
Anthropic: the transformer lets every token attend to every other token across the context, which gives n² pairwise relationships for n tokens.

Pope and colleagues at Google (2022): for a model of over 500 billion numbers with standard multi-head attention, the KV cache for 512 prompts of 2,048 tokens totals 3 TB, 3 times the size of the model itself.
Anthropic: models have an attention budget, and every new token in the context draws it down.
Liu and colleagues (2023) found that language models often use information best when it sits at the start or end of a long prompt, and markedly worse when it sits in the middle.
Larkspur mini's training script follows nanoGPT (MIT), which its author now calls deprecated in favour of nanochat.
The Illustrated Transformer, by Jay Alammar, walks through the Transformer step by step in pictures.
3Blue1Brown's "Attention in transformers, step-by-step" (Deep Learning chapter 6) animates queries, keys, values and masking.
Transformer Explainer, from Georgia Tech's Polo Club, runs GPT-2 small (124M parameters) live in the browser.
